tweets.text:
“I think about time in model generations.

Each one takes 3-4mos. 3 gen ago, I was writing code by hand. So when people ask me what’s going to happen in 2yrs, that’s 8 gens later. I have no idea.”

Sensei @karpathy on the future of AI models. https://t.co/lTLCNap8DR

Most people are wrong here. It IS actually possible to communicate between two airgapped computers with temperature changes, but the data transfer rate is too slow (1-8b/hr) to be effective.

The underlying point Noam makes is true though: there are a deluge of crazy airgapped comms techniques like EM emanations from DRAM clocks that get a lot faster (300kbps).

This isn’t sci-fi. We vastly underestimate what AI can do with perfect knowledge of all of this literature.
